The Visual Analog Scale (VAS) is a commonly used tool in clinical settings to measure subjective characteristics or feelings that cannot be directly measured, such as pain intensity, fatigue, or mood. It typically consists of a straight line, often 10 cm in length, with two endpoints representing extreme levels of the phenomenon being measured.

Ends of the scale: The left end (0) usually represents the absence of the characteristic (e.g., "No pain"), and the right end (10) represents the maximum intensity or severity of that characteristic (e.g., "Worst possible pain").

Patient's response: The patient marks a point on the line that represents their perception of the current intensity. The position of the mark is then measured in millimeters or centimeters.Pain: The VAS might be used to assess pain, with one end of the line representing "No pain" and the other representing "Worst pain imaginable."

The Oswestry Disability Index (ODI) is a widely used clinical tool designed to measure the degree of disability in patients with low back pain. It assesses the impact of back pain on a person's daily activities, quality of life, and ability to function. The ODI is often used in both clinical practice and research to track changes in disability over time, particularly in individuals with chronic or acute low back pain.The ODI consists of 10 questions, each with 6 possible responses. Each question is related to a specific activity or aspect of life that could be impacted by low back pain. The responses are scored on a scale from 0 (no disability) to 5 (maximum disability), and each section is then given a score that reflects the severity of the disability.

raw_primary_outcome_measure: Change from Baseline in Pain Interference as Assessed by the PROMIS SF v1.0 - Pain Interference 4a at 3 months Post-baseline
raw_primary_outcome_description:
The PROMIS Pain Interference - Short Form 4a is a validated, self-report 4-item tool assessing pain interference over the past 7 days. The PROMIS SF v1.0 - Pain Interference 4a consists of 4 questions and uses a 5-point scale, ranging from 1 (not at all) to 5 (very much). The total raw score equals the sum the values of the response to each question. The raw score is converted to a T-score. The T-score rescales the raw score into a standardized score with a mean of 50 and a standard deviation (SD) of 10. A higher PROMIS T-score represents more of the concept being measured. For negatively-worded concepts like pain interference, a T-score of 60 is one SD worse than average. That is, a person has more problems with pain hindering activities. By comparison, a pain interference T-score of 40 is one SD better than average.

Change = 3 month score - baseline score

raw_primary_outcome_description:
To evaluate the effectiveness of an exercise intervention on IBS symptoms as measured by a change in the Fibromyalgia Impact Questionnaire, modified version (FIQ-R) scores from baseline.

The FIQ serves as a tool for assessing and evaluating the condition of patients with fibromyalgia (FM) and tracking their progress and outcomes. Specifically designed to gauge the aspects of health status most impacted by FM, the FIQ comprises ten items. The initial item consists of 11 questions about physical functioning, each rated on a 4-point Likert-type scale. The subsequent items (2 and 3) prompt patients to indicate the number of days they felt well and the days they were unable to engage in work or housework due to FM symptoms. Items 4 through 10 feature horizontal linear scales with ten increments, allowing patients to rate work difficulty, pain, fatigue, morning tiredness, stiffness, anxiety, and depression.

To evaluate the effectiveness of an exercise intervention on IBS symptoms as measured by a change in the IBS-Symptom Severity Scale (IBS-SSS) questionnaire score from baseline.

The IBS-SSS is a validated questionnaire for gastrointestinal symptoms and provides a global measure of symptom severity by assessing five items ("severity of abdominal pain", "frequency of abdominal pain", "severity of abdominal distension", "dissatisfaction with bowel habits", "impact of symptoms on quality of life") on a visual analog scale. The values of the five items are added together to give a total score between 0 and 500. Cases are then classified as 'mild' (75 to 175), 'moderate' (175 to 300) and 'severe' (\>300).

Two experienced neurologists or neuroradiologists will be invited to review the MRI scans independently. Scheltens' visual rating scale will be used to measure the degree of WMAs. Briefly, WMAs will be separately graded in each of the following locations: frontal lobes, temporal lobes, parietal lobes and occipital lobes. Only the women who are identified WMAs (Scheltens' visual rating scores \>0) will take the MRI test again at the 24th week.

raw_primary_outcome_measure: Endogenous pain modulation mechanisms_ Temporal Summation of pain
raw_primary_outcome_description: Change from baseline in the temporal summation (TS) variable of pain, or endogenous pain facilitation. Will be assessed two minutes after the last quantified Pressure pain thresholds (PPT) at both levels (shoulder and calf). Participants will receive 10 pressure pulses perceived as painful, starting at the previously determined mean PPT intensity. Pressure will be increased at a rate of approximately 2 kg/s for each pulse, with 1-second rest intervals between pulses. For each pulse, the pressure will be maintained for 1 second before being released. After the first, fifth, and tenth pulse, participants will be asked to verbally rate their pain on a verbal numerical rating scale (VNRS). The TS measurement variable will be defined as the difference between the VNRS score after the tenth pulse and that after the first pulse

raw_primary_outcome_measure: Endogenous pain modulation mechanisms_Conditioned pain modulation
raw_primary_outcome_description: change from baseline in Conditioned pain modulation (CPM) or endogenous pain inhibition. To assess CPM, the sequence previously described for the temporal summation of pain will be repeated while a so-called 'heterotopic noxious conditioning stimulus' is applied to the patient. This painful stimulus will consist of placing an occlusion cuff on the left arm. The cuff will be inflated to the pressure previously determined to correspond to a verbal numerical rating scale (VNRS) score of 3, representing a moderate pain intensity stimulus. The CPM measurement variable will be defined as the difference between the initial VNRS score before inflating the cuff and the initial VNRS score during cuff occlusion.

The COPM is used to assess individuals' activity performance and satisfaction levels. In this assessment scale, the problems encountered by individuals in the field of activity performance are determined through a semi-structured interview. Individuals evaluate their activity performance problems with their own performance and satisfaction scores. In the first step, individuals are asked to identify the problems in the areas of self-care, productivity and leisure time that they do, want to do or have difficulty in doing in their routine. In the second step, individuals are asked to assign an importance value between 1 and 10 to each of these activities. In the third step, individuals are asked to select up to 5 activities that are most important for them and to give performance and satisfaction scores between 1 and 10 for each activity. The performance and satisfaction scores are totalled and divided by the number of activities to obtain performance and satisfaction scores.

Chronic pain levels will be measured by The BPI-SF is a validated and widely recommended tool for assessing pain severity and pain-related interference in chronic pain patients. It measures pain severity at its worst, least, average, and current level over the past week on a 0-10 scale, with 0 = no pain and 10 = worst pain imaginable. It also evaluates interference across seven domains (general activity, walking, work, mood, relations, sleep, and enjoyment of life), each scored 0-10, where 0 = no interference and 10 = complete interference. Scores can be averaged into the Pain Severity Index and Pain Interference Index. The BPI-SF is responsive to changes in pain over time.

raw_primary_outcome_description: Measured by the Pain self-efficacy questionnaire (PSEQ). The PSEQ assesses the strength of a person's confidence in their ability to function, despite their pain. Patients are asked to rate how confident they are so that they can do each of the 10 activities or functions at present, despite their pain, by selecting a number on a seven-point scale, where zero equals 'not at all confident' and six equals 'completely confident'. Scores on the PSEQ may range from 0 to 60, with higher scores indicating stronger self-efficacy beliefs. Good reliability and validity of the PSEQ has been reported. The test-retest reliability and internal consistency of the PSEQ in two different studies with chronic pain patients were reported as 0.79 and 0.92, respectively.

raw_primary_outcome_description: The Visual Analog Scale (VAS) is a simple, effective, valid, and reliable tool that is internationally recognized for assessing participants' pain intensity. Participants are asked to mark on a 10 cm horizontal line to indicate how severely they perceive their pain. The left end of the scale represents "no pain" (0 cm), and the right end represents "unbearable pain" (10 cm). Assessment is performed by precisely measuring the horizontal distance of the marked point from the left end with a ruler. This numerical value is interpreted as an indicator of the participant's pain severity. A score between 1-3.9 cm indicates mild pain, 4-6.9 cm indicates moderate pain, and 7-10 cm indicates severe pain.

Visual Analog Scale (VAS) is a pain intensity measurement scale. It consists of a horizontal line 10 cm in length. The participants were asked to indicate their average pain over the last month by drawing a line, placing a dot, or marking a point on this line. The value of 10 on the line's right side represents severe pain, while the value of 0 on the left side represents the absence of pain. This indicates that the maximum degree of pain is at the far right boundary, and the minimum is at the far left boundary. The length of the distance between the point the participants mark on the line and the point representing the absence of pain indicates the intensity of their pain. The internal consistency of the VAS scale has been found to be 0.82 .

The Fibromyalgia Impact Questionnaire (FIQ) assesses the global impact and severity of FM across 10 items covering Physical Function, Work Status, and Symptoms (pain, fatigue, stiffness, etc.). The total score ranges from 0 to 100.

The calculation involves summing and scaling the scores from the three components: Physical Function is scored on a 4-point scale (0-3) and the sum is then multiplied by 3; Work Status and Symptoms (rated on VAS/NRS) are scaled to contribute to the final 100-point total.

The FIQ is a disability and severity index: a higher score (closer to 100) indicates a greater impact of fibromyalgia, signifying higher functional disability, more severe symptoms, and a worse quality of life. Conversely, a lower score (closer to 0) indicates a better health status. The primary objective is to observe a significant decrease in this score.

raw_primary_outcome_description:
The Pain Catastrophizing Scale (PCS) is a self-reported questionnaire assessing catastrophic thinking related to pain, including rumination, magnification, and helplessness.

The total score ranges from 0 to 52, with higher scores indicating greater pain catastrophizing (worse outcome).

The Roland-Morris Disability Questionnaire (RMDQ) is a self-reported questionnaire assessing pain-related physical disability in daily activities.

The total score ranges from 0 to 24, with higher scores indicating greater disability (worse outcome).

The Tampa Scale for Kinesiophobia - 11 item version (TSK-11) is a self-reported questionnaire assessing fear of movement and re-injury related to pain.

Total scores range from 11 to 44, with higher scores indicating greater kinesiophobia (worse outcome).

The Central Sensitization Inventory (CSI) is a self-reported questionnaire used to assess symptoms associated with central sensitization.

The total score ranges from 0 to 100, with higher scores indicating greater symptom severity related to central sensitization (worse outcome).

The 36-Item Short Form Health Survey (SF-36) is a generic self-reported questionnaire assessing health-related quality of life across multiple physical and mental health domains.

Each domain score ranges from 0 to 100, with higher scores indicating better health-related quality of life (better outcome).

Movement control performance assessed using the Nine-Item Movement Control Test Battery, which evaluates movement quality during standardized functional movement tasks. Each item is scored according to predefined error-based criteria, and item scores are summed to produce a total score ranging from 0 to 93, with higher scores indicating poorer movement control performance.
raw_primary_outcome_time_frame: Immediately before and immediately after each intervention period

raw_primary_outcome_measure: Change from Baseline in Lumbar Proprioception (Active Joint Position Sense) After 6 Weeks of Intervention
raw_primary_outcome_description: Lumbar proprioception will be assessed by measuring active joint position sense during trunk flexion, lateral flexion, and extension using MATLAB-based angle analysis. The absolute angular error (in degrees) between the target position and the reproduced position will be calculated. Angular error is recorded in degrees, starting from 0° upward. Lower values indicate better proprioceptive accuracy. Higher values indicate impaired proprioception.

raw_primary_outcome_measure: Change from Baseline in Pain Intensity at Rest and During Activity After 6 Weeks
raw_primary_outcome_description: Pain intensity will be assessed using the Numeric Rating Scale (NRS). The scale ranges from 0 to 10, where 0 indicates no pain and 10 indicates the worst imaginable pain. Lower scores indicate less pain.

raw_primary_outcome_measure: Change from Baseline in Lumbar Pressure Pain Threshold After 6 Weeks
raw_primary_outcome_description: Pressure pain threshold will be measured using a handheld algometer (Algometer commander, JTech Medical) and recorded in kg/cm². Higher values indicate greater pain tolerance, while lower values indicate increased pain sensitivity.

raw_primary_outcome_measure: Change from Baseline in Trunk and Hip Muscle Strength After 6 Weeks
raw_primary_outcome_description: Isometric muscle strength of trunk and hip muscles will be assessed using a digital hand-held dynamometer (Lafeyette Instrument®, Lafayette, IN) during maximal voluntary isometric contraction. Strength values are recorded in Newtons (N) or kilograms (kg). Higher values indicate greater muscle strength

raw_primary_outcome_measure: Physical Fitness Assessed by the Short Physical Performance Battery (SPPB)
raw_primary_outcome_description: The Short Physical Performance Battery (SPPB) is a test of lower extremity functioning that combines scores from usual gait speed, standing balance, and chair stand tests. Scores range from 0 to 12, with higher scores indicating better physical functioning.

raw_primary_outcome_measure: Change in Pain Unpleasantness Numeric Rating Scale
raw_primary_outcome_description: Change in acute pain unpleasantness will be measured with an individual item ("How unpleasant is your pain, right now?") rated on a numeric rating scale. Scores range from 0 to 10, with higher scores reflecting greater acute pain unpleasantness.
raw_primary_outcome_time_frame: Immediately before to after 4-minute audio recording

raw_primary_outcome_description: The Credibility/Expectancy Questionnaire (CEQ) is a 6-item self-report measure assessing treatment credibility (items 1-3) and expectancy (items 4-6). Items 1-3 and 5 are rated 0 (not at all credible/logical) to 9 (extremely credible/logical), while items 4 and 6 are rated 0% to 100%; subscale scores are standardized and summed (credibility: 3-27 raw equivalent; expectancy similar), with total scores ranging 6-54 after standardization, where higher scores indicate greater credibility and positive outcome expectancy (better outcome).
raw_primary_outcome_time_frame: Baseline (at enrollment, prior to intervention initiation).

raw_primary_outcome_description: The 3-item version of the Client Satisfaction Questionnaire (CSQ-3) is scored by summing responses from its three core items. It consists of empirically selected items measuring key aspects of service satisfaction, each rated on a 4-point Likert scale (1 = lowest satisfaction to 4 = highest, with directionality adjusted as needed). Total scores range from 3 to 12, with higher values indicating greater satisfaction; no reverse scoring or subscales are required.
raw_primary_outcome_time_frame: Administered at the end of treatment at 8 weeks.

raw_primary_outcome_measure: Modified Patient Global Impression of Change
raw_primary_outcome_description: The Modified Patient Global Impression of Change (mPGIC) adapts the standard single-item Patient Global Impression of Change (PGIC), a validated patient-reported outcome measure of overall perceived change since intervention, by assessing change across six specific domains. Each domain uses a single ordinal item rated on a 7-point scale, coded from 1 = Very Much Improved to 7 = Very Much Worse. Lower scores indicate greater perceived improvement. Domains include coping strategies, physical activity, social activity, level of stress, memory and thinking, and pain, and are analyzed separately.
raw_primary_outcome_time_frame: At end of 8 week program (post test) and again at 3 month follow up visit.

raw_primary_outcome_description: A 100-mm horizontal line where participants mark their perceived level of low back pain intensity, with 0 mm indicating no pain and 100 mm indicating worst possible pain. The distance from 0 to the mark is measured in millimeters and used as the score.

Paint intensity will be assessed using 10 cm Visual Analog Scale, ranging from no pain (0) to worst pain" (10). Participants will mark their perceived pain level on the scale; higher scores indicate greater pain intensity.

Disability will be assessed using the Oswestry Disability Index, version 2.0. The ODI is a self-administered questionnaire consisting of 10 sections, each scored from 0 to 5, with higher scores indicating greater disability in activities of daily living. The total score is converted to a percentage using the formula (total score × 100 / 50), yielding a range from 0 to 100. Scores are interpreted as follows: 0-20 minimal disability, 21-40 moderate disability, 41-60 severe disability, 61-80 crippled, and 81-100 bed-bound or symptom exaggeration/aggravation.

Participants reply to a binary ("Today, did you think about or use any suggestion from the OASIS Study text messages?") and continuous ("How much did you think about or use any suggestion from the OASIS text messages?; response range: 0=not at all, 10=very much) question about intervention engagement. They also indicate how much they believe the texting helped them manage their pain, urge to use opioids, remember to take their medication, and manage their withdrawal symptoms (response range: 0=not at all, 10=very much).

Responding to EMA on 25%, 50%, and 75% of days will indicate a low, medium, and high level of acceptability, respectively. An adapted version of a message fatigue measure and a scale of intervention engagement will be used with a response greater than 3 (1 to 5 scales) on each item representing at least some satisfaction with treatment and will serve as the benchmark for acceptability.

Feasibility benchmarks are assessed continually thoughout the study, beginning with the recruitment rate of eligible participants (≥50% of potential participants) and continuing as quantified by retention at 4 weeks (≥75%), 8 weeks (≥65%), and 24 weeks (≥55%). These data are all proportions and are collected as continuous measures of feasibility as quantified by participant engagement.

Medication for opioid use disorder (MOUD) adherence rate is assessed within individuals. Within-subject adherence will be quantified as ≥80% of days taking MOUD. Six-month between-subject retention rates will be classified using the following ranges based on results from prior studies of buprenorphine and methadone adherence. Buprenorphine: 25% or less = low, 25 to 40% = moderate, and 40% or greater = high. Methadone: 40% of less = low, 40 to 50% = moderate, 50% or greater = high.

raw_primary_outcome_description: The Headache Impact Test (HIT-6) is a 6-item questionnaire evaluating the impact of headaches on daily function and quality of life. The change in total score will be used to measure the reduction in headache burden.

Neck-related disability will be assessed using the Neck Disability Index (NDI). The NDI consists of 10 items, each scored on a 6-point scale ranging from 0 to 5, yielding a total score from 0 to 50. The total score will be converted to a percentage score (0-100%), with higher scores indicating a greater degree of functional disability.

raw_primary_outcome_measure: Low Back Disability (Oswestry Disability Index, ODI)
raw_primary_outcome_description: Low back-related disability will be assessed using the Oswestry Disability Index (ODI). The ODI consists of 10 items, each scored from 0 to 5, resulting in a total score ranging from 0 to 50. The total score will be converted to a percentage score (0-100%), with higher scores indicating a greater degree of functional disability.

raw_primary_outcome_measure: Shoulder Disability (Shoulder Pain and Disability Index, SPADI)
raw_primary_outcome_description: Shoulder-related disability will be assessed using the Shoulder Pain and Disability Index (SPADI). The SPADI consists of 13 items, including 5 pain items and 8 disability items, each rated on an 11-point numeric rating scale (0-10). Item scores are summed to yield a total score ranging from 0 to 130, which is converted to a percentage score (0-100%) by dividing the total score by 130 and multiplying by 100. Higher scores indicate a greater degree of functional disability.

raw_primary_outcome_measure: Knee Disability (International Knee Documentation Committee Subjective Knee Evaluation Form, IKDC)
raw_primary_outcome_description: Knee-related disability will be assessed using the International Knee Documentation Committee (IKDC) Subjective Knee Evaluation Form. The IKDC consists of 18 items covering symptoms, sports activities, and function, of which item 10a is excluded from scoring, yielding a raw score ranging from 0 to 87. The raw score is converted to a standardized score (0-100) by dividing the total score by 87 and multiplying by 100, with higher standardized scores indicating better knee function. For analytical purposes, the standardized IKDC score will be reversed (100 - score), such that higher transformed scores indicate a greater degree of functional disability.

The Oswestry Disability Index (ODI) is a self-completed questionnaire used to assess the level of disability in patients with low back pain. The 7 Types Type 1 - Separate hard lumps (severe constipation) Type 2 - Sausage-shaped but lumpy (mild constipation) Type 3 - Like a sausage with cracks on the surface (normal) Type 4 - Smooth, soft sausage or snake (normal, ideal) Type 5 - Soft blobs with clear edges (lacking fiber) Type 6 - Fluffy pieces, mushy (mild diarrhea) Type 7 - Watery, no solid pieces (severe diarrhea) Evaluation Scale

raw_primary_outcome_measure: Level of perceived pain assessed using the Visual Analog Scale
raw_primary_outcome_description: Level of perceived pain assessed using the Visual Analog Scale (VAS), a validated gold standard for fibromyalgia and allowing for direct and comparable measurement. The Visual Analogue Scale is the most widely used method in medicine to measure the intensity of pain subjectively perceived by the patient. It is usually represented as a continuous line 10 centimetres long, the ends of which indicate two opposite conditions: left end (0): no pain ; right end (10): the worst pain imaginable. The patient fills in the instrument by making a mark on the line at the point corresponding to the pain he or she feels. The operator then measures the distance in millimetres (from 0 to 100) to obtain the score. Interpretation of the Scores (cut-off): based on various clinical studies, the values of the scale are generally divided into 4 ranges: 0 - 4 mm: no pain ; 5 - 44 mm: mild pain ; 45 - 74 mm: Moderate pain; 75 - 100 mm: Severe pain.

raw_primary_outcome_measure: Functional Connectivity (FC) changes within Default Mode Network (DMN)-related regions both interictally and during an anxiety-mediated nocebo challenge
raw_primary_outcome_description: All functional and anatomical 3D high-resolution (HR)-T1-weighted images were preprocessed using the CONN toolbox and Statistical Parametric Mapping 12. The primary aim of this exploratory study was to investigate hypothesis-driven functional connectivity changes using a seed-based approach focused on specific DMN regions of interest. We examined connectivity among predefined DMN seed regions, which were defined using the default atlas implemented in the CONN toolbox. Four core DMN seeds were selected: the posterior cingulate cortex (PCC; MNI/Montreal Neurological Institute space -1, -61, 38), the medial prefrontal cortex (MPFC; MNI 1, 55, -3), the left lateral parietal cortex (LP; MNI -39, -77, 33), and the right lateral parietal cortex (LP; MNI 47, -67, 29). Each seed region was defined as a 6-mm radius sphere centered on the respective MNI coordinates, in line with standard CONN preprocessing defaults, to ensure the reproducibility of the seed-based connectivity analyses.

raw_primary_outcome_description: Pain-related catastrophic thinking will be assessed using the PCS, a 13-item self-report measure that evaluates maladaptive cognitive and emotional responses to pain. raw_primary_outcome_measure: Disability (ODI v2.1a) ODI: Oswestry Disability Index
raw_primary_outcome_description: Change in Oswestry Disability Index total from baseline to 3 months. Time Frame: T0 to T3. Co-primary with BPI-4; both must reach significance. The Oswestry Disability Index version 2.1a (ODI) is a 10-item self-report questionnaire assessing back pain related disability across pain intensity, personal care, lifting, walking, sitting, standing, sleeping, sex life, social life, and travelling. Each item is scored 0 to 5 and the total is converted to a percentage. Scores range from 0 to 100 percent, with higher scores indicating greater disability, so a decrease in score is a better outcome. Proportional scoring is applied when items are missing, per standard ODI version 2.1a scoring. This outcome is the change in ODI total score from baseline to 3 months. It is co-primary with the Brief Pain Inventory Short Form 4-item pain severity subscale (BPI-4); both must reach statistical significance to claim treatment effectiveness.

raw_primary_outcome_measure: Modified Patient Global Impression of Change
raw_primary_outcome_description: The Modified Patient Global Impression of Change (mPGIC) adapts the standard single-item Patient Global Impression of Change (PGIC), a validated patient-reported outcome measure of overall perceived change since intervention, by assessing change across six specific domains. Each domain uses a single ordinal item rated on a 7-point scale: Very Much Improved (coded 1), Much Improved (2), Minimally Improved (3), No Change (4), Minimally Worse (5), Much Worse (6) or Very Much Worse (7). The range per domain is 0 (worst, Much Worse) to 5 (best, Very Much Improved), with higher scores indicating greater perceived improvement. Domains are analyzed individually as mean scores (no total computed), where values \<4 reflect net positive change. Domains include coping strategies, physical activity, social activity, level of stress, memory and thinking, and pain.

raw_primary_outcome_description: TSK-17, full name Tampa Scale of Kinesiophobia-17, ranges from 17 to 68, and a higher score indicates worse kinesiophobia.
raw_primary_outcome_time_frame: TSK-17 was administered at baseline, 8 weeks, 24 weeks.

raw_primary_outcome_description: Patient-reported outcomes measures (PROMIS) Pain Intensity short form 1a to measure reported average pain intensity over the previous seven days using an 11-point Likert scale (0 = no pain; 10 = worst imaginable pain). The minimum value is 0 and maximum value is 10 with higher scores meaning a worse outcome.

Patient-reported outcomes measures (PROMIS) 8-item pain interference measure to collect reported pain interference with various activities in the previous seven days on a scale of 1 to 5 (1 = not at all; 5 = very much); the minimum value is 8 and maximum value is 40 with higher scores meaning a worse outcome.

Monthly enrollment rate and proportion of eligible individuals who enroll in the study. Recruitment feasibility will be evaluated according to prespecified traffic-light progression criteria: green, ≥75% of eligible individuals enrolled or ≥10 participants/month; amber, 50-74% or 5-7 participants/month; red, \<50% or \< 5 participant/month.
Proportion of eligible participants who provide informed consent to participate in the study. Prespecified progression criteria are: green, ≥80%; amber, 60-79%; red, \<60%.
Proportion of randomized participants who complete the primary feasibility assessment time point (T1). Prespecified progression criteria are: green, ≥80%; amber, 60-79%; red, \<60%.

Proportion of planned Psychologically-Informed Physical Therapy sessions completed by participants allocated to the intervention group. Prespecified progression criteria are: green, median adherence ≥70%; amber, 50-69%; red, \<50%.

Proportion of participants with complete datasets for the prespecified secondary outcomes at the primary feasibility time point. Prespecified progression criteria are: green, ≥90%; amber, 75-89%; red, \<75%.

Acceptability of the intervention will be assessed using the Treatment Acceptability and Preferences (TAP) measure, supplemented by brief exit interviews evaluating perceived value, burden, and usability of the telerehabilitation pathway. Higher TAP scores indicate greater treatment acceptability. Prespecified progression criteria are based on TAP scores, with scores ≥12 indicating the green progression category and scores \<8 indicating the red category.
raw_primary_outcome_time_frame: Following the intervention/at the prespecified acceptability assessment point.

raw_primary_outcome_measure: Incidence of Intervention-Related Adverse Events and Serious Adverse Events
raw_primary_outcome_description: Number and proportion of participants experiencing adverse events (AEs) or serious adverse events (SAEs) considered related to the intervention. Events will be documented for severity, causality, actions taken, outcome, and follow-up. Prespecified progression criteria consider both the occurrence of SAEs and the proportion of participants experiencing mild or moderate AEs.
raw_primary_outcome_time_frame: From enrollment through the final telerehabilitation session, up to 12 months.

raw_primary_outcome_description: Proportion of control-group participants reporting exposure to components similar to the PIPT intervention during the study. Prespecified progression criteria are: green, ≤10%; amber, 11-20%; red, \>20%.
raw_primary_outcome_time_frame: Throughout the study period, up to 12 months.

raw_primary_outcome_description: Proportion of scheduled videoconference sessions completed without a technical interruption or dropout lasting more than 5 minutes. Prespecified progression criteria are: green, ≥90%; amber, 80-89%; red, \<80%.

Consistent with the traffic light framework proposed by Avery et al., progression to a definitive RCT will be decided as follows: proceed (green) if ≥6 domains meet green thresholds and no domain is red; amend (amber) if ≤2 domains are red or if 3-5 domains are green; stop (red) if ≥3 domains are red or if a serious adverse event probably related to the intervention occurs alongside an unfavorable safety pattern
raw_primary_outcome_time_frame: At the end of the intervention

raw_primary_outcome_description: Proportion of eligible invited PHC workers who provide informed consent and are randomized. Calculated as the number of participants randomized divided by the total number of eligible workers invited, multiplied by 100. Higher percentages indicate greater recruitment feasibility.
raw_primary_outcome_time_frame: From start of recruitment until completion of recruitment, up to 3 months

raw_primary_outcome_description: Proportion of randomized participants who complete the post-intervention assessment. Calculated as the number of participants completing the post-intervention assessment divided by the total number randomized, multiplied by 100. Higher percentages indicate greater retention feasibility.

Proportion of scheduled FKQ assessments completed by participants. Completion will be assessed for the baseline and post-intervention evaluations. Higher percentages indicate greater assessment feasibility.

Participation in the assigned educational intervention. Receipt of the written educational material will be recorded in both groups. In the experimental group, access to and completion of the asynchronous microlearning video will also be recorded using available platform data or participant self-report when platform data are unavailable.

Pain intensity at rest, during activity, and at night will be assessed using a 100-mm Visual Analog Scale (VAS), ranging from 0 mm (no pain) to 100 mm (worst imaginable pain). Higher scores indicate greater pain intensity.
raw_primary_outcome_time_frame: From enrollment to the end of intervention at 8 weeks

raw_primary_outcome_measure: Change in Central Sensitization Inventory (CSI) Score
raw_primary_outcome_description: The Central Sensitization Inventory (CSI) assesses somatic and emotional symptoms associated with central sensitization. Part A comprises 25 items scored on a 5-point Likert scale ranging from 0 (never) to 4 (always), yielding a total score from 0 to 100. Higher scores indicate greater central sensitization severity, with a score of 40 or higher indicating the presence of central sensitivity syndromes.

Pain intensity was scaled using a 10-centimeter Visual Analog Scale ranging from 0 (no pain) to 10 (extreme pain). Pain is linearly proportional to pain score, and so, change from baseline was assessed for week 8, and a pain score move in the direction of decreasing pain was considered a clinically significant score change in the direction of decreasing pain if the score decreased by at least 2 centimeters to the left on the scale.

The 24-item Roland-Morris Disability Questionnaire was used for the evaluation of back-related disability with a score ranging from 0 to 24 with 24 indicating the highest disability. Roland-Morris scores from baseline to week 8 were analyzed for this study. It was determined a decrease of 3.5 or more points was clinically significant.

Results were positive for lumbar instability or negative for lumbar stability based on the Prone Instability Test. Progressive changes in lumbar stability by way of test results taken at baseline and again at 8 weeks were examined.

raw_primary_outcome_measure: Change in Pain Intensity (Numeric Rating Scale)
raw_primary_outcome_description: Pain intensity will be assessed using the Numeric Rating Scale (NRS), ranging from 0 (no pain) to 10 (worst imaginable pain). Higher scores indicate greater pain intensity. Changes in NRS scores from baseline to post-intervention and follow-up will be evaluated.

raw_primary_outcome_measure: Change in Functional Disability (Roland-Morris Disability Questionnaire)
raw_primary_outcome_description: Functional disability related to low back pain will be assessed using the Roland-Morris Disability Questionnaire (RMDQ). The total score ranges from 0 to 24, with higher scores indicating greater disability. Changes in RMDQ scores from baseline to post-intervention and follow-up will be evaluated.

Number of participants recruited per month and proportion of the target sample (30-40 participants) recruited within the planned recruitment period. Pre-specified feasibility success criterion: \>=75% of the target sample recruited. Participant flow will be reported in a CONSORT 2025 flow diagram, adapted according to the CONSORT extension for pilot and feasibility trials.

Proportion of screened individuals who are eligible, and proportion of eligible individuals who consent to participate and are randomised (%, with 95% confidence intervals). Reasons for ineligibility and refusal will be recorded.

Percentage of scheduled sessions attended (36 exercise sessions and 12 education sessions), per participant and overall, in the intervention group. Pre-specified feasibility success criterion: mean attendance \>=70% of sessions.

Proportion of randomised participants who complete the post-intervention assessment, and proportion of dropouts with reasons, in each group. Pre-specified feasibility success criterion: retention \>=80%.
raw_primary_outcome_time_frame: From randomisation to post-intervention assessment (approximately 16 weeks, including a 2-week holiday break)

raw_primary_outcome_description: Number, type and severity of adverse events, reported as counts and rates per participant and per session, recorded in a structured safety log. Pre-specified success criterion: no serious intervention-related adverse events.
raw_primary_outcome_time_frame: From the start of the intervention to post-intervention assessment (approximately 16 weeks)

raw_primary_outcome_measure: Acceptability: Patient Global Impression of Change (PGIC)
raw_primary_outcome_description: Participant-rated global impression of change in pain and function attributable to the exercise programme on the 7-point PGIC (Portuguese version; 1 = no change/worse to 7 = a great deal better), complemented by a brief study-specific satisfaction and acceptability questionnaire on the programme components.
raw_primary_outcome_time_frame: Post-intervention (within 2 weeks after completion of the 12-week intervention)

raw_primary_outcome_measure: Change in cross-sectional area of lumbar multifidus muscle measured by ultrasound
raw_primary_outcome_description: The cross-sectional area of lumbar multifidus muscle will be measured by B-mode ultrasound. The difference between baseline and post-intervention value will be calculated to evaluate the morphological change of lumbar multifidus muscle after 12-week rehabilitation exercise.

Pressure pain threshold will be measured with a manual pressure algometer at the 18 tender points defined in the ACR fibromyalgia criteria (bilateral occiput, low cervical, trapezius, supraspinatus, second rib, lateral epicondyle, gluteal, greater trochanter, and knee). Pressure will be applied perpendicular to the skin at a steady rate, and the participant will report the moment the pressure first becomes painful. The value at that moment will be recorded at each point. The total algometric score will be calculated as the sum of the values from all 18 points. Higher scores indicate a higher pain threshold (lower pain sensitivity), and an increase from baseline indicates improvement. Measurements will be performed under standardized conditions at baseline and after the 8-week intervention.
raw_primary_outcome_time_frame: Baseline and 8 weeks (after the intervention period)

raw_primary_outcome_measure: Motor Dual-Task Cost During the Timed Up and Go Test
raw_primary_outcome_description: Motor dual-task cost will be calculated as \[(dual-task TUG time - single-task TUG time) / single-task TUG time\] × 100. TUG time will be measured in seconds. During the dual-task condition, participants will count backward by threes while performing the TUG test. Two trials per condition will be averaged. Higher percentages indicate greater deterioration in motor performance under dual-task conditions. The primary comparison will be the post-intervention value adjusted for baseline performance and age stratum.
Change in pain intensity measured on an 11-point Numeric Rating Scale (0 = no pain, 10 = worst possible pain).
Change in disability as measured by the Roland-Morris Disability Questionnaire (RMDQ); total score ranges from 0 (no disability) to 24 (maximum disability).

raw_primary_outcome_measure: Psychological Distress (Depression, Anxiety and Stress Scale-21)
raw_primary_outcome_description: Change in psychological distress levels as measured by DASS-21. Higher scores indicate greater distress.

raw_primary_outcome_measure: Change in Depression and Anxiety Levels Assessed by the Depression Anxiety Stress Scales-21 (DASS-21)
raw_primary_outcome_description: The Depression Anxiety Stress Scales-21 (DASS-21) is a 21-item self-report measure and a shortened version of the original 42-item Depression Anxiety Stress Scales (DASS-42). It consists of three 7-item subscales assessing depression, anxiety, and stress. Each item is rated from 0 to 3. For each subscale, the seven item scores are summed to obtain a raw score ranging from 0 to 21, and the raw score is then multiplied by 2 to obtain the final subscale score ranging from 0 to 42. In this study, the Depression and Anxiety subscale scores are evaluated. Higher scores indicate greater symptom severity and therefore a worse outcome.
raw_primary_outcome_time_frame: Baseline (before the first group session), at the end of the fourth session (up to 1 month) and 1 month after the final session

raw_primary_outcome_measure: Change in Headache Impact Assessed by the Headache Impact Test-6 (HIT-6)
raw_primary_outcome_description: The Headache Impact Test-6 (HIT-6) is a 6-item self-report measure assessing the impact of headache on daily life, including pain, social functioning, role limitations, cognitive functioning, psychological distress, and vitality. Total scores range from 36 to 78, with higher scores indicating a greater negative impact of headache on daily life and therefore a worse outcome.
raw_primary_outcome_time_frame: Baseline (before the first group session), at the end of the fourth session (up to 1 month) and 1 month after the final session

raw_primary_outcome_measure: Change in Health-Related Quality of Life Assessed by the Short Form-12 Health Survey (SF-12)
raw_primary_outcome_description: The Short Form-12 Health Survey (SF-12) is a 12-item measure assessing health-related quality of life. It provides Physical Component Summary (PCS) and Mental Component Summary (MCS) scores. Standardized scores range from 0 to 100, with higher scores indicating better health-related quality of life and therefore a better outcome.
raw_primary_outcome_time_frame: Baseline (before the first group session), at the end of the fourth session (up to 1 month) and 1 month after the final session

raw_primary_outcome_description: Lumbar pain intensity on a 10-cm visual analogue scale (0 = no pain, 10 = worst imaginable pain). Higher scores indicate worse pain.
raw_primary_outcome_time_frame: Baseline and 1 week after the end of the assigned intervention (week 10 in the radiofrequency arm; week 13 in the exercise and combined arms)

raw_primary_outcome_measure: Pain was measured using a visual analogue scale (VAS).
raw_primary_outcome_description: The visual analogue scale consists of a 10-cm line, each labelled at the left end as 'no pain' (0) and at the right end as 'very severe pain' (10).Patients were asked to draw a vertical mark on each line(Delgado et al., 2018).
raw_primary_outcome_time_frame: A total of three measurements were taken (one baseline and two post-tests at 4 and 8 weeks post-intervention).

raw_primary_outcome_measure: Disability was assessed using the Oswestry Disability Index (ODI).
raw_primary_outcome_description: Disability was assessed using the Oswestry Disability Index. It contains ten items related to limitations in daily life activities, rating each on a 0-5 point scale; the points are added together and converted into a percentage:Minimally disabled (0-10%), moderately disabled(20-40%), severely disabled (40-60%), crippled (60-80%) or bedbound (80-100%)(Rocchi et al., 2005).
raw_primary_outcome_time_frame: A total of three measurements were taken (one baseline and two post-tests at 4 and 8 weeks post-intervention).

raw_primary_outcome_measure: Change in Pain Intensity on the Visual Analog Scale (VAS)
raw_primary_outcome_description: Change in headache pain intensity from baseline to the end of the 4-week treatment period, measured using the Visual Analog Scale (VAS). The change will be compared among the four study groups.
raw_primary_outcome_time_frame: Baseline, Week 4 (end of treatment), and Week 8 (1 month after treatment)

raw_primary_outcome_description: Lower-limb functional performance was assessed using the 1-minute sit-to-stand test (1-min STS). Participants were instructed to complete as many full sit-to-stand repetitions as possible in 60 seconds using a standardized armless chair. The outcome was the number of correctly completed repetitions. Higher values indicate better functional performance. Changes were assessed across three time points.

Handgrip strength was measured using a Jamar hydraulic hand dynamometer. Three maximal voluntary contraction trials were performed with the dominant hand, with rest intervals between attempts. The highest recorded value was used for analysis and expressed in kilograms (kg). Higher values indicate greater handgrip strength. Changes were assessed across three time points.

raw_primary_outcome_measure: Change from Baseline in Pain Intensity on the Visual Analog Scale (VAS)
raw_primary_outcome_time_frame: Baseline (T0), post-intervention at 8 weeks (T1), and follow-up at 12 weeks (T2)

raw_primary_outcome_measure: Change from Baseline in Fibromyalgia Impact Questionnaire (FIQ) Total Score
raw_primary_outcome_description: Total score of the Fibromyalgia Impact Questionnaire (FIQ) assessing overall fibromyalgia disease severity and functional impact across three domains: function, overall impact, and symptoms. Total score ranges from 0 to 100, where higher scores reflect greater symptom severity and impact on daily life.
raw_primary_outcome_time_frame: Baseline (T0), Post-intervention at 8 weeks (T1), and Follow-up at 12 weeks (T2)

raw_primary_outcome_measure: Adherence to Home-Based Exercise Maintenance Program
raw_primary_outcome_description: Adherence to the home-based maintenance program (guided by educational brochure and preregistered videos) measured as the percentage of completed prescribed exercise sessions recorded via a self-reported daily exercise log during the 4-week follow-up period. Adherence is calculated as (Number of completed sessions / Total prescribed sessions) \* 100.
raw_primary_outcome_time_frame: Daily during the 4-week follow-up period (from Week 8 to Week 12)

raw_primary_outcome_description: The Beck Depression Inventory (BDI; Beck et al., 1996), consisting of 21 items with four response options (0-4), assesses depressive symptoms. It establishes different quantitative ranges of depression: absent or minimal depression (\< 13), mild to moderate depression (14-19), moderate depression (20-28), and severe depression (\>28). We will use the Spanish version (Sanz et al., 2005), which has adequate reliability (α = .93). It includes two subscales: a cognitive-affective subscale and a somatic-motivational subscale.
raw_primary_outcome_time_frame: Changes will be assessed from pre-treatment to immediately after the intervention, and also at 3-month follow-up

raw_primary_outcome_description: The MLQ is a self-reported questionnaire made up of 10 items, and it was developed to assess the two main dimensions of meaning in life: presence and search for meaning in life. The items are rated on a 7-point scale ranging from 1 (absolutely false) to 7 (absolutely true). The factors of Presence and Search were correlated (r = -.19), and internal consistency was good for Presence (.86) and Search (.87). One-month test-retest reliability coefficients were .70 for Presence and .73 for Search.
raw_primary_outcome_time_frame: Changes will be assessed from pre-treatment to immediately after the intervention, and also at 3-month follow-up

raw_primary_outcome_description: The MEMS assesses the dimensions of meaning in life: Understanding, Purpose, and Significance, with a total of 15 items. Likert-type responses are given on a 7-point scale (1 = Strongly disagree; 7 = Strongly agree). We will use the Spanish version (Marco et al., 2022), where the three MEMS subscales showed adequate internal consistency: Understanding (ϖ = .91), Purpose (ϖ = .92), and Significance (ϖ = .86).
raw_primary_outcome_time_frame: Changes will be assessed from pre-treatment to immediately after the intervention, and also at 6-month follow up

raw_primary_outcome_description: In this study, we used Part A of the PIL, which consists of 20 items with a Likert-type scale (1 to 7). It provides a measure of the level of achievement of meaning in life. Items include: "Life seems completely boring to me," with a Likert-type response (ranging from "1 = completely routine" to "7 = always exciting"). Scores range from 20 to 140 points, with three levels: scores below 90 indicate a level of existential emptiness, scores between 90 and 105 indicate a level of uncertainty regarding the meaning of life, and scores above 105 indicate a level of achievement of meaning. We used the Spanish version (Noblejas de la Flor, 2000), which has adequate reliability (α = .88).
raw_primary_outcome_time_frame: [Time Frame: Changes will be assessed from pre-treatment to immediately after the intervention, and also at 3-month follow up

raw_primary_outcome_description: Validation of the Spanish version of the Pain Catastrophizing Scale in fibromyalgia. Medicina Clínica, 131(13), 487-492. It measures the tendency to have exaggerated negative thoughts about pain, such as ruminating about suffering or feeling hopeless. It consists of 13 items grouped into three subscales: rumination, magnification, and helplessness. It is useful for predicting pain intensity, disability, and response to treatment. A validated Spanish version exists for patients with fibromyalgia and chronic pain with a reliability of (α = 0.79).
raw_primary_outcome_time_frame: Changes will be assessed from pre-treatment to immediately after the intervention, and also at 3-month follow up

raw_primary_outcome_description: Current pain intensity will be assessed using a 0-10 numeric rating scale, with 0 indicating no pain and 10 indicating the worst pain imaginable. Pain intensity will be assessed immediately before and after the intervention; the primary analysis will compare post-intervention ratings across experimental conditions while adjusting for the corresponding pre-intervention rating.
raw_primary_outcome_time_frame: Immediately before and after the 15-minute intervention

raw_primary_outcome_description: Current pain unpleasantness will be assessed using a 0-10 numeric rating scale, with 0 indicating not at all unpleasant and 10 indicating extremely unpleasant. Pain unpleasantness will be assessed immediately before and after the intervention; the primary analysis will compare post-intervention ratings across experimental conditions while adjusting for the corresponding pre-intervention rating.
raw_primary_outcome_time_frame: Immediately before and after the 15-minute intervention

raw_primary_outcome_measure: Change in Pain Intensity (Numeric Pain Rating Scale, NPRS)
raw_primary_outcome_description: Pain intensity rated on a 0 to 10 scale (0 = no pain, 10 = worst pain imaginable). Higher scores indicate greater pain.
raw_primary_outcome_time_frame: Baseline (before intervention), immediately after intervention, and 1 week after intervention

raw_primary_outcome_measure: Recruitment of Eligible Participant and Caregiver Dyads
raw_primary_outcome_description: Recruitment feasibility will be assessed by the number of eligible participant and caregiver dyads enrolled relative to the target sample of 20 dyads. Each dyad consists of one adult with early-stage Alzheimer's disease and related dementias (ADRD) and chronic pain and one eligible adult caregiver. Recruitment will be summarized as the number of enrolled dyads and the percentage of target enrollment achieved, calculated as the number of enrolled dyads divided by 20, multiplied by 100.
raw_primary_outcome_time_frame: Up to 12 months (from initiation of recruitment through completion of enrollment).

raw_primary_outcome_description: Retention will be assessed as the percentage of enrolled participant and caregiver dyads completing planned study procedures, including the intervention period and end-of-study assessments. The retention percentage will be calculated as the number of enrolled dyads completing study procedures divided by the total number of enrolled dyads, multiplied by 100.
raw_primary_outcome_time_frame: From enrollment through completion of study procedures, approximately 2 weeks per dyad.

raw_primary_outcome_measure: Completion of Scheduled Home Listening Sessions
raw_primary_outcome_description: Intervention adherence will be measured as the percentage of scheduled home listening sessions completed by each adult participant with ADRD. Each participant is scheduled to complete eight 30-minute sessions, consisting of two morning MUSIC CARE® sessions, two afternoon MUSIC CARE® sessions, two morning audiobook control sessions, and two afternoon audiobook control sessions. Adherence will be calculated as the number of completed sessions divided by eight, multiplied by 100.
raw_primary_outcome_time_frame: Across eight scheduled home listening sessions over approximately 2 weeks per participant.

raw_primary_outcome_measure: Acceptability of Caregiver-Assisted Home Listening Procedures
raw_primary_outcome_description: Acceptability of the home-based listening intervention and caregiver-assisted study procedures will be evaluated using study-specific information collected from participants with ADRD and their caregivers. The assessment will address experiences with listening sessions, caregiver assistance, equipment setup, remote supervision, and physiological monitoring. Available responses will be summarized descriptively to characterize the acceptability of completing these procedures in the home setting.
raw_primary_outcome_time_frame: During the home intervention period, approximately 2 weeks per dyad.

raw_primary_outcome_measure: Percentage of Artifact-Free EEG Epochs During Home Sessions
raw_primary_outcome_description: EEG acquisition feasibility will be measured as the percentage of recorded EEG epochs retained as artifact-free and suitable for analysis after signal preprocessing and quality assessment. For each session, the percentage of artifact-free EEG epochs will be calculated as the number of usable epochs divided by the total number of recorded epochs, multiplied by 100. EEG will be acquired during five-minute eyes-closed resting periods before and after listening and continuously during the 30-minute listening intervention. At least 50% artifact-free epochs per session is the prespecified feasibility benchmark.
raw_primary_outcome_time_frame: Before, during, and after each of eight home listening sessions over approximately 2 weeks per participant.

raw_primary_outcome_measure: Acquisition of Analyzable Heart Rate Variability Recordings
raw_primary_outcome_description: HRV data acquisition feasibility will be assessed by the completeness and analyzability of heart rate and RR interval recordings obtained using the Polar H10 sensor during home study sessions. Recordings will be evaluated for signal quality and suitability for deriving HRV indices following artifact screening. Data availability and analyzability will be summarized descriptively across scheduled resting and listening recording periods. No numerical HRV feasibility threshold is prespecified.
raw_primary_outcome_time_frame: During resting and listening recordings across eight home sessions over approximately 2 weeks per participant.

raw_primary_outcome_measure: Clinical Effectiveness: Brief Pain Inventory (BPI) Pain Intensity and Pain Interference
raw_primary_outcome_description: Clinical effectiveness outcome measurement tools include Brief Pain Inventory (BPI): Participants will localize their pain through a drop down menu, in which they will select the applicable body part(s) where they experience pain. The BPI Pain Intensity and Pain Interference scales will then be administered. The pain intensity subscale includes 4 pain intensity ratings using an 11-point numerical rating scale (0-10) on current pain, average pain, worst pain during the last 7 days and least pain during the last 24 hours. The pain interference subscale includes 7 interference items that ask the patient to respond using an 11-point numerical rating scale (0-10). These items include the effect on general activity, mood, walking ability, normal work (including housework), relations with other people, sleep, and enjoyment of life.
raw_primary_outcome_time_frame: Baseline, 1 week post-intervention, 1 month follow up.
instruments_detected: Brief Pain Inventory | Numeric Rating Scale

raw_primary_outcome_description: A random selection of participants will be interviewed regarding their PRT experience.
raw_primary_outcome_time_frame: Interviews will be conducted within 6 months of participating in the PRT session.

raw_primary_outcome_description: Clinical effectiveness outcome measurement tools include Pain Self-Efficacy Questionnaire (PSEQ-10): The PSEQ-10 is a validated 10-item tool for assessing the patient's pain self-efficacy or belief in one's capability to perform activities even when undergoing pain. The 10 items ask the patient to rate their confidence in doing activities on a 7-point numerical rating scale (0-6), with higher scores indicating greater confidence.
raw_primary_outcome_time_frame: Baseline, 1 week post-intervention, 1 month follow up.
instruments_detected: Numeric Rating Scale | Pain Self-Efficacy Questionnaire

raw_primary_outcome_measure: Clinical Effectiveness: Patients' Global Impression of Change (PGI-C) Scale
raw_primary_outcome_description: Clinical effectiveness outcome measurement tools include Patients' Global Impression of Change (PGI-C) Scale: The PGI-C is a validated single- item self-report measure used to assess a patient's perceived change in overall status following a treatment or intervention. Patients select one of 7 options to describe their experience, ranging from "very much worse" to "very much improved." The PGI-C is widely used in chronic pain research and has demonstrated sensitivity to clinically meaningful change across a range of pain populations.

raw_primary_outcome_measure: Clinical Effectiveness: Positive and Negative Affect Scale (PANAS)
raw_primary_outcome_description: Clinical effectiveness outcome measurement tools include Positive and Negative Affect Scale (PANAS) PANAS is a validated 20-item self-report measure assessing two distinct dimensions of mood: positive affect and negative affect. Participants rate the extent to which they have experienced each emotion using a 5-point Likert scale (1 = very slightly or not at all, 5 = extremely), with higher positive affect scores and lower negative affect scores reflecting better emotional well-being. The PANAS has demonstrated strong reliability and validity across clinical populations, including individuals with chronic pain.
raw_primary_outcome_time_frame: Day of Intervention, 1 week post-intervention, 1 month follow up.

raw_primary_outcome_measure: Trunk motor control (supine), Pressure Biofeedback Unit
raw_primary_outcome_description: Deep abdominal muscle activation and lumbopelvic stability assessed with a pressure biofeedback unit in crook lying during the abdominal drawing-in maneuver, starting at 40 mmHg. The score is the absolute deviation from 40 mmHg (best of three trials); smaller values indicate better motor control.
raw_primary_outcome_time_frame: Baseline and immediately after the single intervention session

raw_primary_outcome_measure: Trunk motor control (prone; transversus abdominis activation), Pressure Biofeedback Unit
raw_primary_outcome_description: Activation of the transversus abdominis assessed in prone lying with the pressure biofeedback unit placed under the abdomen and inflated to 70 mmHg. Participants draw the abdominal wall in without moving the spine or pelvis. The score is the pressure reduction from 70 mmHg held steadily (best of three trials); larger reductions indicate better activation.
raw_primary_outcome_time_frame: Baseline and immediately after the single intervention session

raw_primary_outcome_measure: Pain Explanation Competence (PEC) on an unseen cross-context transfer scenario.
raw_primary_outcome_description: Study-specific analytic rubric with six domains (scientific accuracy; clarity/comprehensibility; alignment with contemporary pain science/biopsychosocial framework; misconception correction; safe, non-nocebogenic communication; patient/context adaptation), each scored 1-5. Total 6-30; higher = better. Mean of three blinded assessors.
raw_primary_outcome_time_frame: 12 weeks after completion of the 4-week intervention

raw_primary_outcome_measure: Change following Goal Management Training in participant-reported everyday executive difficulties over the follow-up period measured with the Dysexecutive Questionnaire (DEX)
raw_primary_outcome_description: Everyday executive difficulties are assessed using the participant-reported Dysexecutive Questionnaire from the Behavioural Assessment of the Dysexecutive Syndrome. The 20-item questionnaire assesses cognitive, behavioral, and emotional manifestations of executive dysfunction in everyday life. The total score ranges from 0 to 60, with higher scores indicating greater executive difficulties.
raw_primary_outcome_time_frame: Change over time will be evaluated using assessments conducted at baseline, immediately after Goal Management Training, and at 6- and 12-month follow-up.
